X.summary: Most precise and best sourced of the three. Every checked number traces to a primary source, and the only slip is an unconfirmed NeurIPS venue label. It is the only report that brings in the matched-budget scaling study (45% threshold, task-type dependence) and the DeepResearch Bench citation-accuracy counter-evidence, and it separates the two baselines (no-tool model vs tool-using agent) clearly.

Y.summary: Accurate, compact and fully primary-sourced, with no bad citations and one small overreach on how DeepTRACE's range is scoped. It names the compute confound and the vendor-eval issue well, and adds the text-only HLE caveat and the citation-reliability angle. It is thin, though: it leaves out the 45% threshold, error amplification, the co-scientist work and the AI-scientist evidence, so a decision-maker gets less to act on.

Z.summary: Broadest coverage (GAIA, MLE-bench, AlphaEvolve, CORE-Bench, METR horizons, the ideation-execution gap), and every number I checked was correct; it also flags its memory-sourced items honestly. It rests on memory rather than fetched primary pages, gives few URLs, and leaves out the central compute-matched studies (Kim et al. 2512.08296, Tran & Kiela), so its C2/C3 matched-compute verdict leans on older or indirect evidence. It also pads with tangential items such as Snell, More Agents and the IMO results.
